questions.question: An Activity is launched fresh from the launcher. In what order are its callbacks called until the user can interact with it?
questions.explanation: `onCreate` sets up the instance, `onStart` makes it visible and `onResume` makes it interactive (foreground). `onRestart` only runs when a previously stopped activity comes back, never on a fresh launch.

questions.question: `onRestart()` is called only when an activity that was stopped comes back to the foreground, and it runs right before `onStart()`.
questions.explanation: Returning from the stopped state goes `onRestart` → `onStart` → `onResume`. A paused-but-not-stopped activity (e.g. behind a translucent activity) skips `onRestart` and goes straight to `onResume`.

questions.question: Activity A starts full-screen Activity B. In what order do the callbacks of both activities run?
questions.explanation: A pauses first, then B is created and resumed, and only once B covers the screen is A stopped. That is why heavy work in `onPause` delays the next screen, while `onStop` is the better place for expensive cleanup.

questions.question: This enum is declared in the same order as AndroidX `Lifecycle.State`. What does it print?
questions.explanation: Enum comparison uses declaration order. `STARTED` is above `CREATED` but below `RESUMED`, and `DESTROYED` is the lowest state of all, below even `INITIALIZED`, so `isAtLeast(INITIALIZED)` is false for a destroyed lifecycle.

questions.question: The user is on your Activity and presses Home. Assuming the process is not killed, which callbacks run?
questions.explanation: Home sends the task to the background: the activity becomes invisible (`onStop`) but is not finished, so `onDestroy` does not run and `isFinishing()` is false. When the user returns, it goes `onRestart` → `onStart` → `onResume`.

questions.question: Showing an `AlertDialog` (or a `DialogFragment`) from an Activity causes the Activity's `onPause()` to be called.
questions.explanation: A dialog is just another window owned by the same activity, so the activity stays RESUMED. Only another activity coming to the foreground (e.g. a dialog-themed or translucent Activity) pauses it.

questions.question: Fragment A is replaced by Fragment B with `replace(...).addToBackStack(null).commit()`. Which callbacks run on Fragment A?
questions.explanation: Because the transaction is on the back stack, A's view is destroyed but the fragment instance stays alive (CREATED), so `onDestroy` and `onDetach` don't run. Popping the back stack calls A's `onCreateView`/`onViewCreated` again on the same instance.

questions.question: In a Fragment, which is the earliest callback where `requireContext()` is guaranteed not to throw?
questions.explanation: `onAttach(context)` is the first callback and the point where the fragment becomes associated with its host. `onCreate` and later also have a context, but they come after `onAttach`; the symmetric last callback is `onDetach`, after which `requireContext()` throws again.

questions.question: Activity A starts Activity B, which uses a translucent (dialog-like) theme so A is still visible behind it. What happens to A?
options: A gets onPause only and stays visible in the STARTED state
A gets onPause and onStop, because another activity is in front
A gets no callbacks, because it is still visible
A gets onPause, onStop and onSaveInstanceState
questions.explanation: `onStop` only runs when an activity is no longer visible. A partly visible activity behind a translucent one is paused, not stopped, and on returning it goes straight to `onResume` without `onRestart`/`onStart`.

questions.question: The user presses Back on your second (non-root) Activity and nothing intercepts it. Which statements are true?
options: onPause, onStop and onDestroy run on the activity
onSaveInstanceState is called so the screen can be restored later
Overriding onBackPressed() is the recommended way to intercept this
questions.explanation: Back finishes the activity, so it is destroyed with `isFinishing()` true, and no instance state is saved because the user won't return to it. `isChangingConfigurations()` is only true for config-change recreation, and `onBackPressed()` is deprecated in favour of `OnBackPressedDispatcher` with an `OnBackPressedCallback`, which supports predictive back.

questions.question: This Fragment is put on the back stack and later shown again. What is the problem?
options: A second observer is added on each return, and the old one leaks the destroyed view
Nothing, because observers added in onViewCreated are removed automatically in onDestroyView
It crashes, because lifecycle can't be accessed in onViewCreated
The observer never fires, because the fragment's lifecycle is already RESUMED
questions.explanation: `lifecycle` here is the Fragment's own lifecycle, which outlives its view while on the back stack, so each `onViewCreated` adds another observer bound to an old view. Use `viewLifecycleOwner.lifecycle` for anything tied to the view; it is destroyed in `onDestroyView`, which removes the observer.

questions.question: On Android 12 and higher, pressing Back on a task's root launcher activity (with no back callback registered) moves the task to the background instead of finishing the activity.
questions.explanation: Since Android 12 the system keeps root launcher activities alive on Back, so returning to the app is a warm start that doesn't run `onCreate` again. The activity gets `onPause`/`onStop` like a Home press, not `onDestroy`.

questions.question: In an app that targets Android 9 (API 28) or higher, when is `onSaveInstanceState` called as the user presses Home on your Activity?
options: Only in onDestroy, if the process is about to die
questions.explanation: For apps targeting API 28+, it is guaranteed to run after `onStop`. For apps targeting earlier versions it ran before `onStop`, with no ordering guarantee relative to `onPause`, which is why older advice about its timing is unreliable.

questions.question: Which statements about `FragmentTransaction.add` and `replace` on the same container are true?
options: replace removes every fragment currently in that container before adding the new one
add keeps the existing fragments, so their views can end up stacked on top of each other
With replace plus addToBackStack, pressing Back brings back the removed fragment
add can only be used once per container
replace without addToBackStack keeps the old fragment instance alive for later
questions.explanation: `replace` is remove-all-then-add, and `add` leaves existing fragments in place, which is the classic overlapping-views bug. Without `addToBackStack`, the removed fragment is fully destroyed (`onDestroy`, `onDetach`), so nothing is kept for later.

questions.question: Right after `Lifecycle.Event.ON_PAUSE` has been dispatched, what does `lifecycle.currentState` return?
questions.explanation: Events are the edges and states are the nodes: ON_PAUSE moves RESUMED down to STARTED, and ON_STOP moves STARTED down to CREATED. There is no PAUSED or STOPPED state.

questions.question: While an Activity is already RESUMED, you call `lifecycle.addObserver(obs)` where `obs` is a `DefaultLifecycleObserver` that logs `onCreate`, `onStart` and `onResume`. What gets logged?
options: onCreate, onStart, onResume, in that order
Nothing until the next lifecycle event, since RESUMED was already reached
Only onResume, the event matching the current state
questions.explanation: `LifecycleRegistry` brings a new observer up to the current state by dispatching every missed event in order, so a late observer still sees a consistent sequence. `DefaultLifecycleObserver` is the recommended API; the annotation-based `@OnLifecycleEvent` is deprecated.

questions.question: A network callback arrives after the user has sent the app to the background (the Activity is stopped and `onSaveInstanceState` has run). It calls `supportFragmentManager.beginTransaction().replace(R.id.c, ResultFragment()).commit()`. What happens?
options: It throws an IllegalStateException about state loss
The transaction is queued and applied when the activity resumes
The transaction is silently dropped, since the container view is detached
It commits normally, and the new fragment survives process death
questions.explanation: Once state is saved, any change made after it would be missing from the saved state, so `commit()` throws to flag the state loss. `commitAllowingStateLoss()` avoids the crash but can lose the change. A better fix is to hold the result as state and update the UI when the lifecycle is at least STARTED.

questions.question: On a current Android version, two apps run side by side in split-screen and the user taps from app X into app Y. Which statements are true for X's activity?
options: It stays in the RESUMED state
It is no longer the top-resumed activity and gets onTopResumedActivityChanged(false)
It receives onPause because it lost focus
It receives onStop because another app is in front
questions.explanation: With multi-resume (Android 10+), every visible top activity in multi-window stays RESUMED. Focus is tracked separately as the single top-resumed activity, so losing focus doesn't trigger `onPause`, and X stays visible so it isn't stopped.

questions.question: What happens when this transaction runs?
options: It throws IllegalStateException: commitNow can't be added to the back stack
It runs synchronously and adds the entry to the back stack
It runs synchronously, and addToBackStack is silently ignored with a log warning
It behaves exactly like commit(), on the next main-thread frame
questions.explanation: `commitNow()` executes immediately, out of order with any pending `commit()`s, which would corrupt back-stack ordering, so it rejects `addToBackStack`. Use `commit()` for back-stack transactions, and `executePendingTransactions()` if you need them applied right away.

questions.question: If an Activity calls `finish()` inside `onCreate()`, the system calls `onDestroy()` next without calling `onStart`, `onResume`, `onPause` or `onStop`.
questions.explanation: An activity that finishes before it was ever started goes straight from created to destroyed, a common trick for routing activities that just redirect. Cleanup placed only in `onStop` or `onPause` won't run in that case.
